No torrents, no proxies (CP, 8chan browsing, death threats, nasty stuff). You can white-list traffic to certain domains only and set bandwidth caps to prevent abuse. This helps fight net nuetrality.

The problem: Internet networking has changed

In the past you used to be able to just buy a VPN service and you had a new IP. This isn't the case at all anymore. IPs are now of 2 types. Consumer IPs (Residential ISPs and mobile phone ISP IP addresses) and business (classic data centers and big data centers like AWS). If you use a VPN it's a 100% chance they are giving you a data center ISP, and these are easy to either block or make as a second class citizen. So when you go to signup for a gmail or search for hotel bookings or flights or something they see you aren't really a consumer, so you will be treated as a a second class citizen: blocked from making gmails, given fake or old pricing data on hotels and flights (this is how they deal with bots on VPNs).

The solution

Residential and mobile ISPs are in high demand now from well basically everyone. From the most hideous types of people who want to blend in more and use it for CP, to spammers, to more grey area things like scraping, and for people looking just for freedom of political persecution. Right now shady as fuck companies like Hola VPN offer "free VPN" but you have to be an exit node so any nasty fuck searching or accessing CP will send their traffic to exit from your PC and that is the door that the FBI will kick down.   1. Price. Let people be paid in bitcoin to whore out their Res ISP IP address and electricity use for their PC. Free market stuff.
  2. Services offered. The contract will be allow white listing domains and/or ip addresses.

EG: You install either or both an android app or a PC program. Nothing will exit from you yet. You then have to write a service contract to the network, like a job posting basically. You then add a price for both bandwidth and access (EG: $1 to use your IP for up to 24 hours and $1 per GB of traffic). In the contract, you only allow traffic to reach gmail.
